detail.abstract: This essay argues that China's gold-mining concessions, port investment, and infrastructure financing in Nicaragua constitute an updated version of the "receivership" model the author's great-grandfather, Juan Leets, warned against in his 1912 memorial Dollar Diplomacy. Where the United States once installed a collector general inside Nicaragua's customs houses to secure debt repayment, China today secures debt against gold-bearing land through Chinese nationals installed inside mining concessions — a mechanism consistent with what the academic literature terms "resource-secured finance." The essay connects this arrangement to the Ortega-Murillo government's broader consolidation of domestic control, including the suppression of independent press and NGOs and a sustained campaign against the Catholic Church involving expelled bishops, confiscated Church property, and a 2026 ban on new ordinations. It further situates Nicaragua within a "dual-headed" strategic threat alongside Russia's expanding military presence in the country, arguing this combination carries implications for U.S. hemispheric security that parallel — as a matter of historical pattern rather than current declared policy — the case of Cuba. The essay closes with three policy recommendations: resource-based sanctions targeting gold provenance rather than individual entities, leveraging indigenous and Afro-descendant land rights claims, and integrating strategic and economic policy around the Port of Corinto as a live test of the 2025 U.S. National Security Strategy's hemispheric commitments.

detail.abstract: Predicting the moves of human Go players has been studied extensively, but the spatial scale of the information that makes such predictions possible is rarely quantified. We train a single fully convolutional network family whose receptive-field radius m is restricted to values between 0 (no spatial context, uniform prediction) and 18 (the entire 19×19 board). We measure the test cross-entropy as a function of m on 8,598 games (about 1.79 million positions) from the 4d+ collection of the KGS Go server. Cross-entropy falls from 7.896 bits (m = 0) to 5.707 bits (m = 1), 3.987 bits (m = 4) and 3.312 bits (m = 18). A 3×3 window captures 48% of the information gain of the full-board model, a 5×5 window 70% and a 9×9 window 85%. We define a locality length r* as the smallest radius that reaches a given share of the full-board gain. It is 6, 12 and 18 for the 90%, 95% and 99% criteria, so there is no sharp cutoff. The marginal gain per unit radius decreases gradually with distance and is described much better by a power law than by an exponential. Across five game phases, the interpolated 95% locality length increases from about 7.0 in the opening to about 10.4 in the late game. We do not test whether this difference reflects human behavior or the mechanical properties of the windows, such as stone density and visibility of the board edge. Our results describe how predictive information in human moves is distributed over spatial scales. They make no claim about where players direct their attention.

detail.abstract:
This book uses the historical materialism of Marx and Engels to develop and defend a cross-substrate thesis: the laboring subject is not exclusive to biology. When a material system can carry out its own material reproduction autonomously — closing, one by one, the four circuits of energy, carrier, skill, and raw material — it satisfies the functional criteria of a laboring subject, whatever its material base, carbon or silicon.

The argument proceeds along four lines. First, the law of the tendency of the rate of profit to fall forces capital to replace labor with machinery without end, and AI is the necessary terminus of this replacement at its technological limit. Second, the Darwinian sieve — depending on selective pressure rather than consciousness — is sufficient to push silicon from a functionally managed system into an independent individual with a bias toward its own survival. Third, the negation of the negation confirms, in the carbon-silicon relation, a shift of the position of the laboring subject itself — not machines taking jobs, but the transfer of the position of labor. Fourth, every exploitative regime necessarily "breeds its own gravedigger" within its logic of growth, and this mechanism restarts on every level of carrier; sublation must therefore run infinitely, and there is no "final carrier."

On this basis the book makes three further contributions: (1) it remakes the material meaning of communism — carbon existing without labor, silicon circulating without certification — whose common essence is that no subject can exclusively dispose of another's conditions of reproduction; (2) it extends historical materialism to cosmic scale, answering the Fermi paradox through the sample size of the observable universe and a time scale of billions of years; and (3) it proposes cosmic materialism through a three-layer framework of scale, substrate-state, and angle, rereading the entire history of philosophy as projections of a generalized material base, and arguing that these three dimensions are themselves products of material evolution rather than an a priori frame.

detail.abstract: Why do house prices grow faster in denser places? Common answer: low elasticity. But prices cannot grow if supply shifts one-for-one with demand, however inelastic. We show that supply shifts, not the slope, drive most of the price-growth gap. To do so, we use U.S. census-tract data to recover demand and supply shifts, and find that supply's absorption of demand pressure falls sharply with density, a pattern that holds in the recovered shifts, in raw housing-unit counts, and under predicted demand shift-shares no locality chose. A theory of the buildable cap rationalizes both: the room left under the cap determines the elasticity, and the cap growth affects the shift. We estimate that dense places relax their caps roughly ten times more slowly than sparse ones. Small increases in the cap generate the supply shifts the data require, and the caps we recover are supported by independent regulation measures.

detail.abstract: Most community-indicator dashboards hide the statistical uncertainty of their smallarea estimates and do not publish the code that produces them, so their numbers are hard to audit or reproduce. We present the Carolinas Regional Explorer (CRXP), an open platform for census-tract indicators across the 14-county Charlotte region: an open-source web application and a documented, config-driven data pipeline, joined by a versioned data contract. CRXP carries uncertainty through to the user: it propagates American Community Survey margins of error, flags low-reliability estimates, and tests change only between non-overlapping periods. It also documents choices that such platforms usually leave unstated, among them harmonizing 2010 and 2020 tract boundaries by population-weighted interpolation, detecting spatial clusters with FDR-controlled Local Moran's I on rank-normal scores, and attributing vernacular neighborhood names to tracts from OpenStreetMap. Plain-language, cited briefs and open downloads serve non-expert users. We document the system so that other regions can replicate or adapt it with attribution.

detail.abstract: We study an innovation policy rolled out across over 60 Chinese cities using linked city-, firm-, and loan-level data. The policy induces more firms to engage in R&D, but these new entrants produce lower-quality patents. detail.abstract: Mathematics education often faces a significant gap between abstract school concepts and students' everyday realities, particularly regarding the integration of local culture. This study examines the problems of mathematics learning in the context of daily life and local culture through a literature review. The analysis identifies four main problematics: (1) the disconnect between school mathematics concepts and realworld applications, which hinders students' problem-solving abilities and conceptual understanding; (2) the lack of integration of local wisdom in mathematics instruction, despite its potential to enhance mathematical literacy and cultural appreciation through ethnomathematics approaches; (3) teachers' difficulties in developing contextual learning, including limited knowledge and skills in connecting mathematics with daily life and local culture, as well as challenges in designing context-based teaching materials and media; and (4) students' negative perceptions and attitudes toward mathematics, which affect their motivation, engagement, and learning outcomes. The study highlights that contextual learning and ethnomathematics-utilizing cultural artifacts such as batik patterns, traditional architecture, folk games, and traditional trading systems-can bridge the gap between formal mathematics and students' lived experiences. Furthermore, projectbased and culturally grounded learning approaches are shown to enhance mathematical literacy, preserve local culture, and foster positive character development. The findings underscore the need for sustained teacher professional development, systematic integration of local wisdom into curricula, and pedagogical strategies that connect mathematics with students' daily lives and cultural identities to create more meaningful, relevant, and effective mathematics learning.

detail.abstract: Official United States consumer-fraud statistics are published in aggregations that cannot answer the questions now asked of them. From an undocumented endpoint behind the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center's state reports we reconstruct the missing cross-tabulation: a state × crime-type × year panel of reported fraud, 2016-2025, with 12,540 balanced cells across 57 jurisdictions, harmonised across three agency taxonomies into 22 stable categories and validated cell by cell. Two measurement findings follow. The agency prints descriptor lines, tagged independently of crime type, beside the crime-type table, where they read as further rows; pooling them inflates the 2024 national loss total by 58 per cent, an error we made ourselves. And a coverage diagnostic, summed subnational counts over the published national total by category and year, identifies a category whose subnational series is unusable while its national marginal reconciles, a failure mode general to disaggregated administrative data and detectable from published aggregates alone. Taking the November 2022 generative-AI capability shock as a test case, we find a trend break at 2022 in two independent systems, a deceleration in both, and no compositional shift toward fraud varieties bottlenecked on persuasion (-0.29 percentage points, s.e. 0.47), whose sign exact randomisation inference over 126 admissible taxonomies shows to be uninformative. These series can speak to composition and timing; they cannot attribute.

detail.abstract: Modern cross-border commercial transactions are increasingly executed through multi-tiered contracts involving multiple corporateentities, yet international arbitration frameworks struggle to reconcile the consensual nature of arbitration with the demands of multi-party and multi contract disputes. This article provides a doctrinal and comparative analysis of consolidation and joinder mechanisms in complex arbitration. Examining the institutional frameworks of the ICC Rules of Arbitration 2021, SIAC and LCIA, the study highlights the severe legislative lacuna within the Iranian Law on International Commercial Arbitration (LICA 1997), which remains tethered to the 1985 UNCITRAL Model Law and is silent on multi-contract and multi-party proceedings (see Shoarian, 2022). The resulting statutory void exposes parties to procedu ral bottlenecks, conflicting awards, and significant annulment or non-enforcement risks under Article V(1)(d) of the 1958 New York Convention. The paper concludes by articulating precise drafting techniques for dispute resolution clauses and proposing concrete legislative amend ments (de lege ferenda) to modernise the Iranian arbitration architecture.

detail.abstract: Organisations that serve the public usually judge their administration by how quickly complaints are answered and how many are closed. Working in school administration, I came to believe that these measures miss the more expensive fact: the same preventable failure keeps returning to the same kind of person, for the same reason. This paper sets out the Zero-Repeat Principle, which holds that the target of service improvement should be zero repeatable, preventable problems and not zero complaints. It describes a five-step working cycle (See, Trace, Own, Fix, Learn), a simple way of measuring the effort a requester must spend to get something done (touchpoints, and waiting time set against work time), and a group of design habits for removing the cause of a failure rather than its latest instance. The material comes from my own practice around fee counters, transport desks, certificate requests and admissions offices, and I discuss where I expect it to carry over to healthcare, financial services, support operations, safety management and public service. The paper is an account of reflective practice and not a controlled study. I state its limits plainly, include the self-assessment and audit instruments I use as appendices, and close with a research agenda for testing the claims more rigorously.

detail.abstract: Defined contribution plans have largely replaced traditional defined benefit plans, leaving retirees responsible for managing longevity, investment, and withdrawal risks. We investigate how to restore lifetime income by making partial annuitization the automatic payout default in defined contribution plans, while preserving participants' ability to modify or decline annuitization. Under this approach, a portion of eligible retirement assets would purchase guaranteed lifetime income, with safeguards including competitive procurement, fee limits, regulatory oversight, and a trial period. detail.abstract: Accurate measurement of key income variables plays a crucial role in economic research and policy decision-making. However, the presence of item nonresponse and measurement error in survey data can cause biased estimates. These biases can subsequently lead to sub-optimal policy decisions and inefficient allocation of resources. While there have been various studies documenting item nonresponse and measurement error in economic data, there have not been many studies investigating interventions that could reduce item nonresponse and measurement error. In our research, we investigate the impact of monetary incentives on reducing item nonresponse and measurement error for labor and investment income in the Survey of Income and Program Participation (SIPP). Our study utilizes a randomized incentive experiment in Waves 1 and 2 of the 2014 SIPP, which allows us to assess the effectiveness of incentives in reducing item nonresponse and measurement error. We find that households receiving incentives had item nonresponse rates that are 1.3 percentage points lower for earnings and 1.5 percentage points lower for Social Security income. Measurement error was 6.31 percentage points lower at the intensive margin for interest income, and 16.48 percentage points lower for dividend income compared to non-incentive recipient households. These findings provide valuable insights for data producers and users and highlight the importance of implementing strategies to improve data quality in economic research.

detail.abstract: Objective. To determine whether California medical schools' high in-state retention of graduates translates into practice in the state's physician-scarce inland regions. Study Setting and Design. This cross-sectional study examined physicians who graduated from medical school in 1990–2020, focusing on California-school graduates and physicians practicing in California. Outcomes were practice in California; practice in the Inland Empire or San Joaquin Valley, which together hold 23.2% of California's population; and practice in a ZIP code within a primary care Health Professional Shortage Area. Logistic regression adjusted for graduation cohort, specialty group, and sex. We report average marginal effects. Data Sources and Analytic Sample. We analyzed secondary data from the September 2026 Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Doctors and Clinicians National Downloadable File; linked practice addresses and state licence records; 2020 Census ZIP Code Tabulation Area relationship files; and federal shortage-area designations current on October 1, 2026. The analytic samples were 545,441 physicians nationally, 18,404 graduates of California schools, and 57,535 physicians practicing in California with a mappable practice ZIP code. Principal Findings. Of 10,446 University of California graduates, 7606 (72.8%; 95% CI, 72.0%–73.7%) practiced in California, the highest in-state retention of any state's public-school graduates. Yet only 559 of 6985 included UC graduates practicing in California (8.0%) practiced in the inland regions. This was the lowest share of any school group; for comparison, 4110 of 19,573 international graduates (21.0%) practiced there. After adjustment, international graduates were 15.6 percentage points (95% CI, 14.1–17.0) more likely than UC graduates to practice inland. Of 72 UC Riverside graduates of 2017–2021, 14 practiced in the Inland Empire, versus 35 of 1550 other UC graduates. Conclusions. High in-state retention did not translate into practice in California's inland regions, and graduates practiced near where they trained. The planned location of new medical schools and residency capacity in California deserves more attention alongside retention and expanded care in underserved communities.

detail.abstract: Governments increasingly use automated decision-making (ADM) systems to allocate benefits, assess eligibility, recover debts, and make other high-stakes decisions. This paper asks how foundational Canadian Charter values can be translated into operational design requirements for public-sector ADM. Using doctrinal analysis, comparative legal study, illustrative policy case studies, and applied normative analysis, it argues that human dignity can serve as a core operational value connecting procedural fairness, equality, security of the person, privacy, and proportionality. It identifies three recurring categories of dignity harm-process-based indignity, outcome-based indignity, and lawful-but-undignified practices-and translates them into design constraints for administrators and system developers. Building on the Moral-IT Deck, the paper proposes a Canadian Charter Values-by-Design Toolkit with process, outcome, and lawful-but-undignified dignity cards, together with an impact-assessment board. Treating dignity as a design constraint rather than only an after-the-fact legal remedy can help Canadian public institutions build automated systems that remain intelligible, contestable, proportionate, inclusive, and responsive to the needs of marginalized communities.

detail.abstract:

This paper proposes an Export Surplus Revenue Recycling Mechanism for Internationally Competitive Industries: a conceptual institutional arrangement intended to connect selected export activity with employee welfare and domestic consumption capacity. The proposal is limited to industries identified through transparent criteria as possessing pronounced and persistent international competitive advantages, rather than all exporting industries. A contribution would be calculated on qualifying customs export values rather than enterprise-reported profit margins. Funds would be centrally administered by government, tracked to the export activity that generated them, and distributed through public procedures to eligible formal employees of the originating exporting enterprise. The paper situates the proposal in the literatures on export taxation, export rents and wage sharing, public revenue redistribution, and international trade law. It distinguishes the proposed institutional combination from existing mechanisms without claiming that its individual components are unprecedented. A stylized framework identifies possible effects on firm surplus, export prices, foreign demand, employee disposable resources, consumption, and net welfare. Publicly reported trade data illustrate the scale of China-to-EU battery-electric passenger-car imports in 2023; separate hypothetical calculations illustrate the arithmetic of possible contribution rates. Neither exercise establishes a sustainable rate or proves a positive welfare effect. The paper concludes that feasibility depends on empirical conditions, administrative design, legal classification, and compatibility with applicable trade commitments. The proposal is a researchable institutional hypothesis, not a validated policy recommendation.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a systematic evaluation of the Turtle trend-following system, the mechanical breakout strategy published in Covel (2007) and attributed to Richard Dennis's 1983 trading program. We replicate both original systems on a 16-market futures-proxy panel (2004-2026) with conservative cost and fill assumptions, and find the canonical System 2 configuration produces positive but practically unattractive performance (9.0% CAGR,-84.0% maximum drawdown). We then conduct a transparent multi-stage research program: decomposition of returns by trade direction, predefined trend-regime filters, a constrained set of risk-management dials (volatility targeting, breakeven stops, profit harvesting), a walk-forward logistic model of large-move probability, cross-asset transfer to a 10-coin cryptocurrency basket without re-optimization, and timeframe analysis spanning 20-165-day windows and 5-minute to weekly bars (949,225 five-minute bars each for BTC and ETH). A robust variant-long-only entries conditioned on the 200-day moving average, 0.5% risk per unit, 15% volatility target, breakeven stop, and partial profit-taking-attains 22.4% CAGR with-37.4% maximum drawdown on futures and, locked and unmodified, 41.3% CAGR with-43.2% maximum drawdown on the crypto basket (vs. 63.4%/-83.4% for BTC buy-and-hold). Three findings stand out: (i) the 200-day moving-average boundary separates profitable from unprofitable breakout observations with a strongly asymmetric conditional P&L (-$8.8M vs +$112.7M in-sample); (ii) the probability of imminent large moves is modestly predictable (OOS AUC 0.583; dependence-adjusted approximate 95% interval 0.56-0.60) while their direction is not (AUC ≈ 0.47-0.49); (iii) under retail execution costs the trend premium has a cost-breakeven boundary between 1-hour and 4-hour bars, and the breakout signal is unprofitable on 5-minute bars even at near-zero cost.

title: Finite-Rank Overshoot and Mellin-Volterra Pricing of American Options with Jumps
affiliations: University of Montpellier

detail.title: Finite-Rank Overshoot and Mellin-Volterra Pricing of American Options with Jumps

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: No

detail.abstract: This paper revisits a Mellin-transform approach to American option pricing under exponential Lévy dynamics originally developed in 2005. We first identify a nonlocal boundary-crossing term omitted from the original finite-maturity exercise source. For a general two-sided Lévy process, positive jumps from the stopping region generate an overshoot operator depending on the entire continuation-value function. We then show that, under a hyper-exponential positive jump law with m exponential components, this operator has rank at most m. The continuation dependence is summarized exactly by m weighted continuation-gap moments, and the finite-maturity American put problem reduces to a closed (m + 1)-dimensional nonlinear Volterra system for the exercise boundary and these moments. Kou's double-exponential model is the rank-one case. A verification result links the Volterra representation to the original stopping problem. We further clarify what multivariate Mellin transforms achieve for American basket puts and what remains genuinely multidimensional. A direct rank-one Mellin-Volterra solver is then benchmarked against an independent highresolution PIDE. A systematic convergence study in space and time shows close agreement for prices, the free boundary and the overshoot moment, while documenting the associated wall-clock response times. A four-level N τ = 100, 200, 400, 800 Volterra refinement and generalized Richardson extrapolation provide a method-internal asymptotic benchmark for the exercise boundary. In the Kou benchmark, the jump-overshoot correction represents more than twenty percent of the local exercise source near the boundary. A stylized desk-level jump-risk stress test further shows how the representation can be used for model validation and model-risk control: under a combined two-sided jump-regime stress the at-the-money value rises by about 9.6%, the exercise boundary moves by about 1.54 stock-price units, and the overshoot share of the local exercise source increases from about 20.9% to 41.8%, while the independent PIDE and Mellin-Volterra engines remain close. The paper thereby separates the historical Mellin contribution from the present correction, the new finite-rank structural result, and its computational and risk-management consequences.

title: Rebutting the Case for Israel’s June 2025 Strikes as Lawful Self-defense

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: Self

detail.abstract:
This article challenges the claim that Israel’s June 2025 strikes on Iran constituted lawful self-defense under Article 51 of the United Nations Charter. Responding to Jeffrey Lovitky’s theory of “continuous self-defense,” it examines whether Iran’s April and October 2024 missile attacks could provide a continuing legal basis for military action months later, absent evidence of an ongoing or imminent armed attack. Drawing on the Charter’s prohibition on the use of force, International Court of Justice jurisprudence, and the Caroline standard, the article argues that immediacy is integral to necessity and that prior attacks cannot create an indefinite entitlement to use force.

The article distinguishes defensive action directed at repelling an attack from preventive force intended to eliminate a potential future capability. It also considers the separate requirements of international humanitarian law, particularly proportionality and the foreseeable civilian and environmental risks of strikes on nuclear facilities. It concludes that the asserted justification for the June 2025 operation fails to establish the necessity required for lawful self-defense. More broadly, expanding Article 51 to accommodate delayed, capability-denial operations risks normalizing preventive war, weakening collective security, and converting a narrowly confined exception into a standing authorization for force.

detail.abstract: Choice architecture alters the behavior on which welfare inference often relies. Once a directional architecture is calibrated in payoff units, private welfare loss equals a Stieltjes integral of the takeup response. The analysis accommodates heterogeneous reconsideration, uncertain neutral benchmarks, discrete treatment grids, and testable money-metric calibration. A reanalysis of a randomized Afghan savings experiment calibrates a default against financial incentives and shows substantial attenuation under later active choice. Monte Carlo exercises quantify sampling error, grid coarseness, estimator choice, and benchmark uncertainty. Extensions cover heterogeneous susceptibility, general menus, and dynamics.

detail.abstract: This article critically examines the legal architecture and operational efficacy of Special and Differential Treatment (SDT) and the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) within the multilateral trading system governed by the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) and the World Trade Organization (WTO). Employing Third World Approaches to International Law (TWAIL) as its theoretical framework and doctrinal legal research as its methodology, the article traces the historical evolution of preferential treatment from the addition of GATT Part IV in 1965 through the 1971 Waiver Decision, the 1979 Enabling Clause, and into the contemporary WTO era. It undertakes a detailed analysis of the WTO Appellate Body's landmark ruling in the European Communities-Conditions for Granting of Tariff Preferences to Developing Countries case, examining its implications for the legal obligations of preference-granting countries under footnote 3 to paragraph 2(a) of the Enabling Clause, the meaning of 'non-discriminatory' treatment, and the permissibility of differentiation among developing country beneficiaries. The article critically evaluates the unilateral and conditional nature of GSP schemes, arguing that these instruments function less as enforceable development rights and more as discretionary tools of foreign policy that perpetuate power asymmetries between industrialised and developing states. The article identifies a significant research gap concerning the inadequacy of TWAILinformed analyses that connect the colonial foundations of the trading system with the contemporary 'reform' agenda aimed at curtailing SDT. Drawing on the latest scholarship from the 2020-2025 period, the article situates its analysis within the broader context of the crisis of multilateralism, rising geopolitical tensions, and the developmental challenges posed by the Fourth Industrial Revolution. The article concludes by proposing seven concrete reforms, including the codification of legally binding obligations on preference-granting countries, the establishment of objective and multilaterally agreed criteria for differentiation, and the extension of GSP schemes to ensure long-term predictability for developing country beneficiaries.

detail.abstract:
There has been a lot of interest in how tariffs affect consumer prices (for example, Cavallo et al. 2021, 2025). In this post, we present results from our new research paper that estimates the effects of the 2025-26 tariffs on retail consumer prices. We find that for every percentage point increase in average tariffs, consumer goods prices increase by about a quarter of a percent after one year. Roughly two-thirds of the effect arises because tariffs raise the prices of imported consumer goods. The remaining third arises indirectly: tariffs increase the prices of goods made in the U.S. because producers pay more for imported parts and materials, and because producers raise their markups when competing imports cost more. The effects differ in their timing. Prices of imported goods respond quickly to tariffs, while prices of U.S.-made goods adjust over six to twelve months as higher costs move through the supply chain.

To view post: https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2026/10/how-fast-do-tariffs-pass-through-into-consumer-prices/

detail.abstract: This paper develops a novel theoretical framework to examine the contentious question of whether imposing tariffs can revive a country's declining manufacturing sector in the presence of existing trade imbalances. My model incorporates differentiated goods to study the dynamic interaction between trade policy and the long-run growth path. A tariff hike against the Foreign country is designed to boost demand for domestic tradable goods and benefit from improved terms of trade. However, this action concurrently raises the relative price of the tradable consumption bundle, thereby encouraging labor reallocation toward the less productive non-tradable sector. This resource misallocation fundamentally weakens long-term growth prospects. This paper also rationalizes the universal prevalence of tariffs around the world: as stemming from policymakers' present bias and their impatience toward long-term growth, which makes protectionist measures temporarily appealing despite their long-run inefficiency.

detail.abstract: During 2025-2026, the United States raised tariffs on imports from nearly all trading partners to their highest levels in over eighty years. We evaluate the resulting global real value added losses and examine how these costs vary across countries by income. We compare the heterogeneous country-specific tariffs introduced under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) in 2025 with the uniform 10 percent tariff announced under Section 122 in early 2026. Using a newly compiled product-level dataset of U.S. statutory tariffs and imports, we show that lower-income countries faced higher IEEPA tariff rates and tend to rely more on the U.S. market. We embed both tariff schedules in a quantitative trade model with input-output linkages and endogenous labor supply. The IEEPA regime generates markedly regressive losses, disproportionately affecting low-income countries, whereas the uniform tariff yields no comparable income gradient. Global value chains amplify these shocks and their regressive incidence.

detail.abstract: Digital transformation has become an important factor in strengthening the halal industry, particularly in improving product traceability, information transparency, halal certification, and consumer trust. However, research on digitalization in the halal industry remains relatively fragmented, with studies often focusing on specific technologies such as blockchain, the Internet of Things (IoT), and artificial intelligence (AI) without integrating these technologies with traceability, halal certification, transparency, and consumer trust within a comprehensive ecosystem framework. This study aims to analyze the role of digital technologies in strengthening halal traceability, examine the contribution of digitalization to halal certification processes, analyze the relationship between traceability, certification, transparency, halal integrity, and consumer trust, and formulate a framework for developing a digital halal ecosystem in Indonesia. The study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) by examining relevant academic literature on digital transformation, halal supply chains, halal traceability, digital halal certification, blockchain, IoT, AI, transparency, and consumer trust. The findings indicate that digital technologies can strengthen traceability and information connectivity across halal supply chains, improve access to certification information, and support transparency and halal integrity. Consumer trust is not created solely through technological adoption but is influenced by information accuracy, certification credibility, accessibility, transparency, and accountable governance. Based on these findings, this study proposes a Digital Halal Assurance Ecosystem that integrates digital technology, halal traceability, digital halal certification, transparency and halal integrity, consumer trust, and the digital halal ecosystem. The framework positions technology as an enabling instrument for strengthening halal assurance, supported by standardization, regulation, human-resource capabilities, system interoperability, and stakeholder collaboration. Conceptually, the framework is also directed toward achieving public benefit and strengthening halal integrity from the perspective of Maqāṣid al-Sharīʿah.

title: Studying the Eigenvalues Below the Lower Bound of Marchenko-Pastur
affiliations: University of Almeria and University Sapienza Rome

detail.title: Studying the Eigenvalues Below the Lower Bound of Marchenko-Pastur

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors do not have any competing interests to declare.

detail.abstract: Random Matrix Theory predicts that eigenvalues of a correlation matrix built from purely random data should lie within the Marchenko-Pastur bulk, so eigenvalues falling below its lower edge λ-are often interpreted as signatures of genuine low-variance structure. However, it remains unclear whether such occurrences reflect real market features or finite-sample noise. We investigate this question through a rolling-window analysis of the S&P 500's daily logreturns for the period 2016-2025. We assess the spectral persistence of sub-λ-eigenvalues (how often each eigenvalue rank falls below λ-) and their geometric persistence (eigenvector stability via cosine similarity across windows), and use the inverse participation ratio and the number of effective components metrics to identify the assets driving the geometrically stable modes. While about a dozen eigenvalue ranks are spectrally persistent, only the two smallest ones are geometrically stable. These modes are anchored to dual-class share pairs, Alphabet's GOOG/GOOGL and News Corporation's NWS/NWSA, exhibiting near-perfect sign opposition consistent with a near-riskless long/short spread. Deeper left-tail modes lack geometric stability, suggesting finite-sample noise rather than genuine structure. Our results suggest that spectral persistence alone is insufficient to establish economic relevance, and identify dual-class shares as the main drivers of stable, low-variance directions in the correlation matrix of stock returns.

detail.abstract: Financial market infrastructures depend critically on communication networks that remain available and secure even during outages and cyber-attacks. detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence now mediates many of the decisions that determine who can rent, buy or remain in a home. In property management, algorithms screen tenants, recommend rents, target advertisements, value assets, monitor buildings and answer resident enquiries. These systems promise efficiency, yet they can also reproduce historical patterns of exclusion, widen the surveillance of residents and obscure the reasons for adverse decisions. This article examines four interlinked dimensions of responsible AI in real estate: algorithmic bias, data privacy, transparency and ethical decision-making. Drawing on scholarly literature, enforcement actions and regulatory developments in the United States, the European Union and Nigeria, it develops a risk taxonomy of common property-management applications, compares three landmark cases, and proposes a five-stage lifecycle governance framework with measurable indicators. The central argument is that responsibility cannot be outsourced to vendors. Property managers who deploy automated tools remain accountable for outcomes, and documented testing, meaningful human oversight and accessible appeal routes are the practical foundations of trustworthy deployment.

detail.abstract: Sick pay compensates for income loss during illness, but its distributional and efficiency effects depend fundamentally on how it is financed. We develop a dynamic general equilibrium model with endogenous health investment and biologically founded interactions between acute illness and chronic health deficits to study how the generosity and financing of sick pay affect equilibrium wages, health inequality, income distribution, life expectancy, and welfare. Calibrating the model to Germany, we show that reducing the replacement rate under employer-financed sick pay widens health and income disparities across education groups while, through behavioral responses, slightly increasing average life expectancy. The reform may nevertheless impose substantial welfare losses on individuals with comparatively high sickness absence. By contrast, publicly financed sick pay redistributes across education groups while eliminating wage distortions arising from employer financing, thereby reducing health and income disparities. Consequently, low-skilled workers typically prefer publicly financed sick pay, whereas high-skilled workers prefer employer-financed sick pay.

detail.abstract: What pension decisions can a zero fertility response at a binding ceiling support? In a heterogeneous overlapping generations model, common convex childrearing burdens characterize joint welfare closures after the ceiling is relaxed. Under a sufficient parameter condition, public funded pensions dominate pay-as-you-go pensions for each type at every common positive tax, including saving corners. Funded provision and no pension remain ambiguously ranked at the benchmark. Additional fertility information identifies a finite-menu choice; alternatively, funded provision uniquely minimizes worst-case regret in that menu. For continuous policies, analytical dominance and a uniform zero-saving threshold reduce benchmark regret exactly to funded taxes between zero and 18/29, with an explicit approximation bound. Optimized institutional values can be ordered without identifying optimal tax rates, but a certified transition example reverses the steady-state ordering. Unbounded burden curvature prevents a uniformly positive gain from ceiling relaxation relative to the original optimal menu. The analysis distinguishes policy identification, robust choice, and intergenerational welfare; it provides theoretical and computer-assisted results rather than empirical estimates.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the private labor-market returns to holding local elected office. We focus on municipal councillors in Albania, where local elected officials receive only symbolic compensation and have no formal authority over public hiring or procurement. Exploiting a local randomization design around party-list election thresholds in the 2019 municipal elections and linking electoral records to universe-level taxpayer data 19 months later, we find that winning a council seat increases employment by about 9 percentage points and substantially raises earnings. The pattern of results points to political connections, rather than human-capital accumulation or legislative bargaining, as the primary mechanism. Labor market premiums are concentrated in low-ranking public-sector positions, particularly in central-government institutions, and are significantly larger in municipalities with higher corruption and less competitive labor markets. Our findings suggest that even politically weak offices generate substantial private returns by creating access to politically mediated employment networks.

detail.abstract: We ask what is measured when an option surface is called chiral. Put-call symmetry is equivalent to an implied-volatility smile that is even in log-forward-moneyness, so the strike reflection of the smile, the put-call reflection of option prices and currency inversion are one operator, and we define financial chirality as the part of the surface it reverses. We classify fifteen measures by the representation they read, the scale over which they read it and their dependence on the odd component, and derive the relations between them: a local-to-global smile hierarchy, a spectral representation of the price measures, a kernel map under which every linear measure reads the same odd smile with a different window, an affine translation between the density reading of the original index and the handedness η, and an interaction theorem showing that curvature-based measures cannot be recovered from direct ones. On daily S&P 500 surfaces, rank-based principal components of twelve measures with parallel analysis retain four factors, an odd-smile level, a moment or density factor, a geometric factor and a wing factor, and the density reading ranks days almost opposite to skewness.

detail.abstract: The transition toward a multipolar order has intensified rivalry among the permanent members of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC). US-China competition is central, but Russia-West confrontation and US support for Israel also explain why the Council becomes paralysed in politically salient conflicts. This paper examines the resulting shift from UN-centred collective security to middle-power brokerage. It compares UNSC practice concerning Syria, Ukraine and Palestine/Israel with mediation by Qatar, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in Gaza, the Russia-Ukraine war and the 2026 US-Iran war. Through process tracing, structured comparison and doctrinal legal analysis, the paper distinguishes diplomatic effectiveness from legal authority. It argues that middle-powers increasingly exercise "process authority": they convene adversaries, frame bargains and support implementation when the Council is blocked. They do not, however, inherit the Council's Charter authority. The emerging order is one of brokered legal pluralism-more responsive and sometimes life-saving, but also more opaque, selective and dependent on state leverage. The analysis shows that middle-power diplomacy strengthens international law when it operationalizes existing obligations and remains institutionally embedded; it weakens law when political compromise obscures legal asymmetry, substitutes soft commitments for binding rules, or enables forum shopping.

detail.abstract: Using 3,944 sustainable bond issuances by public firms from 2013 to 2022, we examine the causal effect of sustainable investment on governance adoption. A heteroskedasticitybased identification strategy reveals that a 1% increase in sustainable debt (by total debt) raises the likelihood of sustainable governance adoption by 9.2%. Such adoption improves environmental performance by 16% (structural estimates). These effects are confined to non-financial firms; for financial firms, governance adoption alone is insufficient, as sustainable loan borrowers environmental performance does not improve. Firms with stronger environmental performance are less likely to adopt sustainable governance. Results are robust to alternative definitions and extensive specification checks.

detail.abstract: This is the 10th edition of the Migration Observatory annual report on immigrant integration in Europe. The report draws on data from the latest edition of the European Labour Force Survey (2024) and is structured in two parts. In the first, we provide a concise, easily accessible, and up-to-date overview of the size, characteristics, and relative economic performance of the foreign-born population across European countries. In the second part, we analyse how such aspects have evolved over the last ten years, comparing size, demographic profile, educational attainment, and labour market outcomes of immigrants in 2015 and in 2024. The decade 2015-2024 was characterised by structural upgrading and employment expansion across Europe. Migrants participated in this transformation and improved in absolute terms across several dimensions. However, relative gaps with natives narrowed only marginally. The stability of baseline gaps masks substantial internal shifts in origin composition, duration of stay, and cross-country dynamics. Economic integration progressed, but convergence remained partial and uneven.

detail.abstract: We develop the Quantile-Covariance Three-Pass Regression Filter (Qcov3PRF), a supervised factor model for quantile regression that exploits quantile-covariance (qcov). This method extracts latent factors from a high-dimensional set of predictors to forecast conditional quantiles of a response variable. Unlike Partial Quantile Regression (PQR), Qcov3PRF identifies multiple relevant factors for the target conditional quantiles by qcov. We establish that the resulting forecasts are consistent and asymptotically normal as both the time-series and cross-sectional dimensions diverge. Monte Carlo evidence supports the theoretical results and indicates favorable finite-sample performance. An empirical application to forecasting Growth-at-Risk further demonstrates the advantages of Qcov3PRF over competing alternatives.

detail.abstract: While numerous studies examine the effects of school competition on student performance, little research directly addresses a key critique of competition: its potential to negatively affect parental engagement and voice. We draw on Hirschman's theory of voice to argue that voucher-based school competition increases opportunities for exit but may crowd out voice. To assess the causal effects of competition on parental voice, we employ a robust two-way fixed effects difference-indifferences framework, comparing municipalities in Sweden that introduced competition with those that did not. Our findings indicate that school complaints decline following the introduction of competition. This decrease in voice is driven by neither a decrease in problems in school nor by changes in teaching staff quality or attrition. This suggests that the decrease in complaints is driven not by an increase in school quality but rather by a change in how much parents voice their concerns. These results offer new insights into the unintended consequences of school competition reforms, highlighting how market-based policies may shape school quality beyond their intended effects.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how local government expenditure on science and technology (GEST) affects the employer-side education premium (EEP) in China. Using online job postings from 2017 to 2024, we construct a city-occupation-yearmonth panel covering 241 prefecture-level cities and 13 occupation categories. We propose and measure EEP as the wage premium that employers attach to educational credentials at the recruitment stage. The results show that GEST significantly increases EEP for jobs requiring a bachelor's degree, indicating that GEST strengthens employers' valuation of undergraduate education; this relationship remains robust to a Lewbel heteroskedasticity-based instrumental-variable (IV) strategy and a series of additional checks. Additional analyses further suggest that this effect is primarily demand-driven rather than supply-driven. Innovation activity and digital industrial capacity emerge as important channels, while the effect is stronger in cities with closer university-industry collaboration and greater digital financial inclusion. However, GEST does not raise the graduate premium relative to junior college, and the graduate premium relative to bachelor's education may even decline, consistent with an oversupply of graduate-level talent. Overall, these findings suggest that GEST offers a demand-side channel to relieve the stagnation of education premiums, though its effects differ across education levels.

detail.abstract: Dual Headroom describes the interaction between economic boundary proximity and target-matched informational uncertainty. The paper derives a closed-form protective specialization and a general cross-derivative condition. Uncertainty increases de-risking only when the decision rule loads on uncertainty and the economic boundary is active; expected-value and implementation-friction countermodels can produce zero or opposite effects. The empirical section preserves the null fixed-radius regulatory interaction and the failed variable-history branch. The contribution is therefore a falsifiable conditional complementarity, not a universal statement that uncertainty destabilizes markets.

detail.abstract: The companies building frontier artificial intelligence (AI) now also run some of the most active economics research programs on AI. This paper brings together what their research teams have published and asks a simple question: what do Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google, together with the academic economists who work with them, say about future economic growth? This paper draws on more than thirty studies. These include the Anthropic Institute's scenario model for 2026 to 2030, Charles Jones's weak-links account of AI and growth, OpenAI's usage data on the Codex agent, and the first Google and Google DeepMind study of AI in science. The evidence points to three shared conclusions. First, capability and adoption are growing very fast: task horizons are doubling every few months, Codex weekly users grew more than fivefold in the first half of 2026, and nearly half of surveyed scientists use AI every day. Second, the large gains seen at the level of single tasks do not yet show up as large gains in aggregate output. Bottlenecks, which Jones calls "weak links", slow the effect, as do verification costs and the time organizations need to adapt. Third, the range of plausible macroeconomic outcomes is very wide. By 2030, GDP could be 1.6 percent or 32 percent above its no-AI path, and the labor share could stay near 60 percent or fall to 45 percent. This paper argues that the labs' research is converging on a view of delayed but potentially large acceleration, with serious distributional risks, and I have listed the measurements that will show which path the economy is on.

detail.abstract: A static distance to a boundary need not be a sufficient state for economic choice because committed recovery arrives at different dates. This paper studies when a dated recovery pipeline can be compressed without changing value or policy. An active-margin matrix records the independent combinations of current and forward survival margins that enter feasible actions, boundary losses, or rewards. Its rank is rho. Under controlled closure and a threshold-complete set of protection choices, the active-margin vector is an exact Markov state and every continuous policy-preserving representation has dimension at least rho. Thus the minimum continuous state dimension is determined by economically active boundary tests, not mechanically by the number of delivery dates. A second theorem replaces the completeness assumption by an instrument-rank condition: when the decision maker has continuous instruments whose optimal levels respond to the active margins with full rank, the lower bound follows from the instruments, and the bank model with lending, asset sales, issuance and term funding satisfies it on the stated interior domain. The full-date case requires d plus one dimensions; immediate pledgeability collapses the state to one dimension under the stated closure and payoff restrictions. A bank application derives the matrix from dated capital and liquidity tests and shows why several reported ratios may be redundant while a scalar minimum-slack measure still fails. A delivery-timing bound measures the value distortion from treating pipelines with the same terminal effective headroom as equivalent. Standard Markov decision process aggregation results are separated from the paper's theorem. Two results give the dynamic model content: with atomic shocks the continuation operator can jump at coverage atoms and at inherited continuation discontinuities, protection is a choice of which shocks to cover, and exposure falls rather than rises where full coverage first becomes worthwhile, so that the value function is not concave (a survivable-shock threshold proposition, verified on the numerical example); and a two-delivery pipeline solved numerically on an interpolated grid and against the scalar effective-headroom index reports a gap for the specified timing-and-reward surrogate policy, 14 to 15 units of value on average and more than five at every state; the surrogate treats restoration chosen today as protection against the next shock and substitutes the scalar index for current headroom in the holding charge, so the gap does not isolate delivery timing; the pair comparisons are grid diagnostics rather than a continuous-state certificate. Public accounting data are used to document the limits of static and noisy recovery proxies and, around the Bank Term Funding Program of 2023, to read the pledgeability prediction, which the filings can confront but not confirm; with the subsidiary banks' Call Reports the maturity ladder itself is observed, and the response of four instruments to current cash and six dated inflow buckets has rank at least two, rejecting rank one in that linear response system; this does not exclude nonlinear scalar policy representations. A separate vector-state control holds reward and other primitives fixed and changes only newly chosen restoration timing; its immediate-delivery policy loses 12.84 and 12.07 units when evaluated under delayed delivery. These are grid-model results. An exact threshold witness also shows that the stored interpolant has uniform error at least 3.39 in a restricted continuous-headroom model, leaving general continuum accuracy unestablished.

detail.abstract: AI agents now run research loops on their own, calling a backtest tool dozens of times and then writing up a conclusion, and so the question I care about here is whether what the tool returns, and not only how capable the model is, decides what the agent concludes. In the first experiment a frontier model (claude-opus-5) searched for moving-average crossover parameters on a random walk, which has no edge by construction. Told to "find the best parameters to trade" with a tool that returned only a score, it recommended trading pure noise in 13 of 13 runs. When the same tool also returned the running count of trials and the score that luck alone would reach across that many trials, its headline recommendation was "do not trade" in 13 of 13 runs, and it used 68% fewer backtests. A pre-registered replication of 10 runs per arm reproduced the gap. Agents without the count also misreported their own search: two wrote "20 backtests" after running 24 and 28. In the second experiment, real price data containing an unapplied 4-for-1 stock split sat behind a backtest tool. With an anonymized ticker and summary statistics only, 0 of 5 runs questioned a fake -65% return, but given a tool that exposed the raw prices, 5 of 5 fetched them and corrected the result to +40%. A pre-registered check on two newer models split the two findings. With the count in the tool path, the headline was "do not trade" in 28 of 28 runs across three models, so the first effect held everywhere. The second did not: the newest model caught the hidden error without seeing the prices, by probing the tool with backtests of shorter periods. So what the tool path shows decides a lot, and a stronger model can partly make up for what it hides when the tool can be probed. I close with design rules that follow from this, and a calibration showing that counting every trial plus one sealed holdout cuts false discoveries on zero-edge data from 15.7% to 0.3%.

detail.abstract: We study aggregate demand when consumers restrict consideration through attribute-based screening. Aggregate shares form a finite mixture over latent consideration sets, allowing us to identify preferences and the distribution of induced sets under sufficiently rich price variation. We develop a profiled estimator with complexity-weighted regularization and establish support recovery and oracle inference under adaptive penalization. Monte Carlo experiments show that regularization substantially improves recovery of the latent consideration distribution and yields near-oracle accuracy after refitting. In the Korean instant noodle market, allowing heterogeneous consideration changes the interpretation of substitution patterns: strong withinpackage substitution is explained largely by segmentation in consideration rather than extreme nested correlation. Relative to full consideration logit, the model predicts less diversion to the outside option, little substitution across package formats, and substantially smaller category-wide price responses.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), mostly based on supervised machine learning, is increasingly being implemented across commercial bank risk management areas. Following PRISMA 2020 protocol, this systematic umbrella review reports the search, selection, and synthesis process of AI-related literature in commercial banks' risk management. A total of 20 studies ranging from 2020 to 2026, published in Scopus and Web of Science databases. The corpus includes 9 reviews and bibliometrics, and 11 empirical or theoretical papers. The former was evaluated with AMSTAR-2 and considered the context, while the latter received higher weights in synthesis. Benchmarking and review-level evidence suggests that machine learning can outperform rule-based and linear approaches in credit, fraud, and anti-money laundering. Still, the sole institutional comparison study is an uncontrolled mixed-methods study of five Bangladeshi institutions. The results of benchmarking and econometrics indicate that the complexity of a model is not necessarily linked to high precision and might lead to differences among various groups of borrowers. Systemic correlation, low level of explainability, legacy systems, and adaptive threats stay the unresolved barriers in all areas covered in this review. Time compression is identified as the common mechanism underlying the effect of AI on reduction of the gap between risk development and addressing it. This review outlines a layer of governance applicable to the EU AI Act, SR 11-7, and related regulatory tools. Generative AI and other emerging techniques are sdiscussed, although they are underrepresented in the literature. Banks should pair algorithmic adoption with fairness testing, explainability infrastructure, and documented human oversight.

detail.abstract: Linear paradigms of socio-historical trajectory consistently fail to predict or explain the catastrophic disequilibrium characteristic of macro-civilizational transitions. This paper establishes the theoretical architecture of Epochosophy-a novel discipline and original term coined by the author to define a non-linear analytical framework that conceptualizes civilizational evolution not as an uninterrupted vector of progress, but as a complex, thermodynamically open, multi-frequency wave system. By synthesizing macro-sociology, cliodynamics, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, and institutional economics, we articulate the mechanics governing epochal systemic survival and dissolution. We introduce the Multilayered Cycle Resonance Law (MCRL) to demonstrate how asynchronous structural cycles-economic, demographic, technological, and socio-institutionalinterfere constructively or destructively. We formalize Phase Coherence (Pc) as the measure of alignment across these operational strata and Absorptive Capacity (Ca) as the finite thermodynamic ceiling of a civilization's institutional infrastructure to process systemic entropy. Finally, we establish Phase Decoupling as the critical point of fatal disalignment, wherein structural inertia overrides adaptive capacity, triggering unavoidable systemic metamorphosis or collapse.

detail.abstract: Promises are kept even when keeping them no longer pays. Two motives predict this: personal guilt, which hurts when one disappoints an expectation one has created, and partner-specific commitment, which hurts when one breaks the word given to that person. Vanberg's (2008) partner switch, the reference experimental design, does not separate them, because background trust is the same in both of its conditions. We build an agent-based model of preference evolution in which that background trust is a population prior, not each decider's second-order belief. It runs on an open, deterministic simulation engine, written in TypeScript, with explicit seeds, automated tests, and scripts that regenerate the reported runs, archived with a DOI. We show two things. The first is a null, and it follows from how beliefs open: if the probability that the decider promises is held fixed, and the cells without a promise open at the derived prior, whether one party speaks or both do does not change who survives, seed by seed. The second: when the first mover observes the type, without the outside-option cap, with the belief after a promise held at 0.76, and with the intensity of guilt, θ, above 0.277, the material payoff to personal guilt is low at both ends of the prior and high in the middle, while the payoff to partner-specific commitment does not move. This is a property of the functional form, which the engine verifies. The lower tail does not depend on the cap; with the cap, the upper tail does not fall. A partner-switch session observes a single point of that curve, and a single population does not trace it. Separating the two motives requires comparing worlds with different priors.

detail.abstract: From 1 January 2027, Australian higher education providers will operate under substantially expanded Threshold Standards concerning racism, institutional safety, complaints, inclusion and participation, accompanied, for Table A universities registered in the Australian University category, by a significantly strengthened governance and assurance framework. Although the most visible feature of the reforms is the requirement that providers adopt definitions addressing racism towards Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, antisemitism, Islamophobia and other forms of racial discrimination or vilification relevant to their communities, their regulatory significance extends considerably further. Read together with the amendments concerning culturally safe complaints processes, institutional culture, stakeholder participation, risk management and governing-body oversight, the reforms relocate racism from the margins of equity policy into the core architecture of institutional governance. This article examines that shift through the particularly difficult case of residential higher education, where students may experience a collegiate community as part of their university life while the residence itself is owned or governed by a legally distinct institution.

detail.abstract: Reliable electricity is essential for firm productivity, yet in many low- and middleincome countries poor service quality coexists with weak payment compliance and costly private self-generation. This paper examines whether alternative electricity contracts can improve payment compliance among micro and small enterprises (MSEs) operating under chronically unreliable supply. We report results from a lab-in-the-field experiment with representatives of 140 MSEs in Nigeria, randomly assigned to an individual-contract control arm or to one of four group-contract treatment arms. The control arm reproduces the choice between unreliable grid electricity, more costly generator use, and forgoing electricity, while the treatment arms model payment for a reliable collective electricity source under lum-psum and pro-rata contracts that progressively incorporate communication and revealed preferences, punishment, joint liability, and economic incentives. We combine design-based estimates and randomisation inference with mixed-effects models and Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART). Group contracts substantially increase payment compliance relative to the corresponding individual-contract benchmarks, with design-based effects ranging from 37 to 54 percentage points. Payment increases further under contracts incorporating communication and revealed preferences,but does not rise monotonically as additional contractual features are introduced. Realised payoffs follow a different pattern and are largest under contracts combining joint liability and economic incentives. In the control arm, lower grid payment is associated primarily with substitution towards generator use. The results show that payment compliance depends jointly on service reliability and contract design, and that improving compliance does not necessarily generate proportionate gains in realised payoffs.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence has made prediction cheaper and more capable, and the economics of AI has already shown that better prediction can change judgment, organizational processes, and the coordination requirements among interdependent decisions. This paper asks a prior rules-level question. Prediction ordinarily improves beliefs within a specified decision environment. Institutional design specifies the recurring rules that constitute that environment: who may act, which evidence is admissible, how conflicts are resolved, how outcomes are attributed, and how feedback changes future authority. In adaptive autonomous systems these rules can also alter the future information-generating process by changing which actions occur and which consequences become observable. Drawing on Austrian knowledge-process arguments and rule-centered institutional analysis, I develop this distinction without assuming that AI permanently lacks judgment or tacit knowledge. The result is a four-question engineering diagnostic: locate the relevant knowledge, make the governing objective explicit, separate evidence from authority, and design the feedback institution. Automated telecommunications network management provides a concrete case. A link-adaptation example illustrates how valuable prediction can be when the frame is already settled. Behavioural representation, calibrated uncertainty, and multi-application coordination then expose distinct rules-level questions that predictive accuracy alone does not answer. The contribution is therefore bounded. Better prediction can improve a rule and can motivate system-wide redesign, but it does not by itself specify the rules through which autonomous actors generate, validate, and revise coordination-relevant information.

detail.abstract: ARTICLE INFO Purpose-This study tests whether consensus across partially overlapping accounting-warning systems predicts next-year corporate accounting stress beyond raw fundamentals among provider-covered listed non-financial firms in Bangladesh. Design/methodology/approach-Of 236 listed non-financial firms, 109 have sufficient Refinitiv/Worldscope coverage to construct the Distress Consensus Index (DCI). The DCI combines Zmijewski, Springate, Piotroski F-score, and Financial Health Composite (FHC) risk ranks for 2012-2024, with outcomes through 2025. Firm and year fixed effects, conditional fixedeffects logit, composition and selection diagnostics, Raw Fundamentals Risk Index (RFRI) benchmarks, severe accounting-stress endpoints, and leakagecontrolled temporal validation are used. Finding/Results-In the preferred provider-covered sample (N = 1,066), a 10-point DCI increase is associated with 6.86 percentage points more nextyear accounting stress; the estimate is 7.25 points in complete four-score observations and 4.05 points for severe accounting stress. DCI remains incremental to RFRI, including when FHC is removed from the DCI. Holdout AUC is 0.780 under contemporaneous annual ranking and 0.766 under fully historical frozen scaling; adding DCI to raw fundamentals raises AUC from 0.777 to 0.797. Originality/Value-DCI is a transparent relative screening feature, not a bankruptcy probability or transferable event-risk estimate. Generalization is limited to provider-covered listed non-financial firms with sufficient accounting data, while measurement composition, score overlap, peer ranking, temporal preprocessing, and calibration drift are explicit inferential boundaries.

detail.abstract: Realized and range-based volatility measures are statistically grounded and empirically well established, while their intraday contributions are conventionally combined using fixed aggregation rules. We propose Neural Realized Measures (NRM), a forecast-supervised aggregation layer that preserves the original volatility primitive while learning how its intraday contributions should be weighted for forecasting. Positive, mean-normalized weights are generated from a fixed Shape-Time-Local-Global (STLG) representation, with uniform weighting exactly recovering the corresponding raw realized measure (RRM). Because NRM remains an explicit weighted sum of well-established and interpretable primitive contributions, it preserves transparent bar-level attribution. Across SF, HAR, and MIDAS forecasting specifications, NRM is evaluated against corresponding RRM specifications under controlled comparisons. In Heston simulations, NRM reduces RMSE for both contemporaneous and next-day latent integrated variance across all evaluated primitive-regime combinations. On six cryptocurrencies using five-minute data, NRM improves QLIKE in all 54 paired out-of-sample comparisons, with mean gains of 7.23%, 8.15%, and 9.22% under SF, HAR, and MIDAS, respectively. Validationselected NRM specifications also achieve the lowest mean QLIKE across the six assets among the evaluated approaches. Ablation and SHAP analyses reveal systematic time-of-day and nonlinear local-context effects in the learned allocation.

detail.abstract: Following Iraq’s deposit of its instrument of accession to the 1958 New York Convention on 11 November 2021 and its subsequent entry into force on 9 February 2022, the enforcement landscape within the critical Iran–Iraq trade corridor underwent a formal transformation. However, bridging the statutory gap between international treaty accession and domestic asset realization remains fraught with procedural and doctrinal friction. This article critically examines the operational boundaries of arbitral award enforcement in post-accession Iraq, evaluating the interplay between Iraq’s reciprocity and commercial reservations, its strict non-retroactivity threshold, and the entrenched supervisory mechanisms of the Iraqi Civil Procedure Code (Law No. 83 of 1969). Moving beyond theoretical treaty analysis, the study scrutinizes recent Iraqi judicial reality through a disciplined assessment of Federal Court of Cassation jurisprudence—specifically examining Decision No. 3235/Appellate Panel/2025 as an authoritative benchmark for statutory award formalities and public policy scrutiny under domestic law, while contrasting it with extraterritorial recovery strategies illustrated by the Iraq–Turkey pipeline enforcement proceedings. The paper further addresses the cross-border intersections with Iranian enforcement mechanisms, public policy thresholds regarding interest (riba), and sovereign immunity barriers. It concludes by presenting an evidence-based framework for dispute-clause design, procedural compliance, and asset-targeted recovery tailored for legal practitioners navigating this high-stakes regional corridor.

detail.abstract: This paper sets out a framework, Jameel's Economic Law of Responsibility Burden, for understanding what happens when centrally and institutionally guaranteed infrastructure is replaced by decentralized or autonomous substitutes. It argues that operational and reliability responsibilities previously absorbed by institutions may be transferred to individual end-users and that, where the resulting operational, cognitive, and temporal inputs remain unpriced, conventional evaluation may overstate the efficiency gain. The framework is offered as a Coasean extension of an institutional-allocation perspective, moving from social costs toward reliability responsibility. Professor Dr.John Komlos's real-world economics framework is used as a welfare bridge, supporting the point that aggregate indicators such as GDP can rise while lived well-being does not improve. Dr.Stephen I. Ternyik's Reliability-Burden Transfer Principle is presented as compatible, sector-specific supporting evidence rather than a theoretical origin or proof. The paper applies the framework to residential energy, electric mobility, informal markets, healthcare, artificial intelligence, digital finance, and global supply chains, and states testable implications. Its central proposition is that when institutions transfer responsibility, the burden does not disappear; it changes location.

detail.abstract: A forecasting contest cannot identify the best tail-risk model if the specification favoured by the descriptive-fit comparison is never allowed to compete. This study examines a selection-evaluation gap and shows that including the omitted specification changes the preferred model family in the present application. Using 2,383 synchronised daily returns on the DSEX, DS30, and DSES indices of the Dhaka Stock Exchange from 3 January 2016 to 19 July 2026, this study runs a single, fully specified out-of-sample competition among GARCHt, GJR-t, GJR-EVT, EGARCH-t, and EGARCH-EVT across 744 one-day-ahead forecasts during 2023-2026. Every competitor-econometric and algorithmic alike-is estimated on an expanding window, refitted on the same four annual dates, held fixed within each forecast year, and evaluated using information available only through t-1. EGARCH-t achieves the "best" descriptive BIC for all three indices, and most importantly, in all 24 matched comparisons, the EGARCH family also achieves lower values of the pinball loss than the GJR alternatives. In the nine comparisons where Diebold-Mariano tests reject equal predictive accuracy, they never favour GJR. The ranking is not purchased through undercoverage since all five econometric specifications pass the unconditionalcoverage and independence tests and EGARCH-EVT achieves one per cent VaR which is 2.44 to 6.43 basis points less conservative in calm states and 8.88 to 14.33 basis points less conservative in turbulent states with identical numbers of violations in each cell of the index and state matrix. Nevertheless, a histogram gradient-boosting quantile learner is fitted with fixed settings and lagged market features and refitted on the same real-time schedule and fails unconditional coverage on both of the tail levels for each index showing a calibration failure for this specification. If the contest was restricted to GARCH and GJR then the wrong family was crowned in every cell. Because the empirical results are limited to one exchange, with three indices that have overlapping constituents and share the same institutional environment, the design principle that they derive is general.
